question:
A clean metal cathode of work function $\phi=2.0\,\text{eV}$ is illuminated normally by monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda=400\,\text{nm}$. Assume the emitted photoelectrons are non-relativistic.

Let $p_\gamma$ be the momentum of an incident photon and $p_{e,\max}$ be the maximum momentum of the emitted photoelectrons.

Using $hc=1240\,\text{eV\,nm}$, $h=6.63\times10^{-34}\,\text{J\,s}$, $m_e=9.11\times10^{-31}\,\text{kg}$ and $1\,\text{eV}=1.60\times10^{-19}\,\text{J}$, determine the ratio $\dfrac{p_{e,\max}}{p_\gamma}$.

(You may assume the lattice absorbs the recoil momentum, so the electron momentum is determined only by $K_{\max}$.)
